scope: Proposition 2.6 (Hecke action and transfer) of the manuscript “Ramanujan-Arthur Decompositions of Cuspidal Functions at Full Finite Level” (preprints/Ramanujan-Arthur-Decompositions-of-Cuspidal-Functions-at-Full-Finite-Level-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 014 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b4b0cfe23007d159), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 14. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose that L has a central label at a closed place x. The operators in Equation (2.3) give the usual affine Hecke algebra at x, with parameter qx, on H•K(L). They give ordinary Hecke operators on H•K(1). More explicitly, let Hw denote the operator with characteristic function 1IwI and Iwahori volume one. Then H2 s = (qx − 1)Hs + qx, HwHw′ = Hww′ if ℓ(ww′ ) = ℓ(w) + ℓ(w′ ). The positive normalized Bernstein translations are Ta = (−1)ℓ(ta) χJa , Ta = q−ℓ(ta)/2 x Hta (a positive), (2.4) and extend multiplicatively to the entire translation lattice. For a standard parahoric P ⊃ I, its two level transfers identify the hyperspecial or parahoric trace cohomology with the image of eP =   X w∈WP qℓ(w) x   −1 X w∈WP Hw. At hyperspecial level the spherical character action agrees with the Bernstein center. The individual-leg slides commute with these actions and transfers. On the Wakimoto graded terms the Bernstein action is the translation action tensored with the weight multiplicities in Theorem 2.3. The Wakimoto filtration gives long exact sequences equivariant for these Bernstein translations and for the selected-leg slides. Its graded terms carry the stated translation action. Thus flat completion, ordered-weight projections, and spectral projectors may be applied to these cohomology sequences. There is also the following geometric form of the rank-one assertion. If an exact trans- lation position is parallel to the simple wall of s, the operator Hs + 1 on its path trace is pullback and sum along the finite etale family of Frobenius-fixed rank-one refinement flags, of degree qx + 1. Consequently Hs takes the sum over the other flags.
